name: MVR Hamburg (Müllverwertung Rugenberger Damm)
capacity_note: 320,000 t/yr MSW; CHP (electricity + steam + district heat); Rugenberger Damm, Hamburg-Altenwerder port
operator: MVR Müllverwertung Rugenberger Damm GmbH & Co. KG (Stadtreinigung Hamburg / Remondis 49%)
source: Klean Industries MVR profile; Stadtreinigung Hamburg MVR page; ITAD plant register; calc: 320 kt × 0.56 t CO₂/t MSW × 0.50 biogenic fraction
notes: Operational since 1999. Steam sold to industrial customers; electricity and district heat to Neuwiedenthal. No confirmed CCS. Hamburg WtE fleet totals ~5 plants; MVR is the dedicated MSW facility. Germany exploring CO₂ storage framework (KSpG reform 2024) — medium retrofit score.

name: MHKW Frankfurt am Main Nordweststadt
capacity_note: 525,600 t/yr MSW; ~28 MWe + 500,000 MWh/yr heat; Frankfurt Nordweststadt industrial zone
operator: MHKW Müllheizkraftwerk Frankfurt am Main GmbH (FES 50% + Mainova AG 50%)
source: GEM Wiki Frankfurt Waste-to-Energy power station; MHKW Frankfurt company profile (HRB 56310); FES Frankfurt subsidiaries page; calc: 525.6 kt × 0.55 t CO₂/t × 0.50 biogenic
notes: District owned by City of Frankfurt and Mainova. Generates ~200,000 MWh electricity and ~500,000 MWh heat. No CCS announced. Hydrogen blend trial for CO₂ reduction reported 2024 (partial fossil-CO₂ mitigation only). Frankfurt has stated no plans for WtE CCS as of 2026.

name: GML Gemeinschafts-Müllheizkraftwerk Ludwigshafen
capacity_note: 390,000 t/yr; 2 × 20 MWe (40 MWe total); Bürgermeister-Grünzweig-Str. 87, Ludwigshafen
operator: GML Gemeinschafts-Müllheizkraftwerk Ludwigshafen GmbH (MVV Umwelt stake)
source: MVV Energie TREA/GML profile; Steinmüller Babcock modernization announcement; CEWEP GML strategic comms; calc: 390 kt × 0.56 t CO₂/t × 0.50 biogenic
notes: Two modern incineration lines; modernized ~2018–2019 (Steinmüller Babcock). Process steam to BASF Chemiepark Ludwigshafen — large industrial steam customer adjacent to site. Strategic location near BASF could enable CO₂ utilization co-located with chemical synthesis.

name: AVA Augsburg (Abfallverwertungsanlage)
capacity_note: 350,000 t/yr residual + 90,000 t/yr biowaste; ~25 MWe; includes biowaste AD fermentation plant
operator: AVA Abfallverwertungsanlage Augsburg GmbH & Co. KG (ZAW public authority)
source: AVA Augsburg WtERT best practice case study; GEM Wiki AVA Augsburg power station; ZAW Augsburg public reports
notes: Integrated WtE plus biowaste anaerobic digestion — biogenic fraction higher than typical MSW-only plants due to organic waste fraction. ~90,000 t/yr biowaste separately fermented for biogas. Combined biogenic CO₂ is correspondingly higher. No CCS confirmed.

name: MVA Bonn Müllverwertungsanlage
capacity_note: ~180,000 t/yr MSW; steam exported to adjacent Stadtwerke Bonn CHP plant for electricity + district heat generation
operator: MVA Müllverwertungsanlage Bonn GmbH (Stadtwerke Bonn subsidiary)
source: Returo MVA Bonn facts & figures; Returo WtE plants page; Bloomberg MVA Bonn profile
notes: Steam-only model: MVA produces steam, adjacent SWB CHP converts to electricity (~97,000 MWh/yr) and district heat (~182,000 MWh/yr). Smaller throughput than other German WtE plants. No CCS plans.

name: TREA Leuna (Thermische Restabfallbehandlungs- und Energieverwertungsanlage)
capacity_note: 390,000 t/yr (2 × 195,000 t); 2 × 20 MWe; process steam to InfraLeuna/Chemiepark Leuna
operator: MVV Umwelt Asset GmbH (MVV Energie AG subsidiary)
source: MVV Energie TREA Leuna EfW plant page; Hitachi Zosen Inova TREA district heat press release; Envi-Con reference Leuna; calc: 390 kt × 0.56 × 0.50 biogenic
notes: Co-located with InfraLeuna Chemiepark — process steam sold to large industrial complex with numerous chemical manufacturers. Operational since 2005, expanded 2007. District heat extraction system added by Hitachi Zosen Inova. Chemiepark proximity is interesting for potential CO₂ utilization.

name: EEW Knapsack Hürth
capacity_note: 320,000 t/yr RDF/SRF; ~118,000 MWh/yr electricity; Knapsack Chemiepark near Cologne
operator: EEW Energy from Waste GmbH (Knapsack plant)
source: EEW Knapsack plant page; GEM Wiki Germany WtE register; calc: 320 kt × 0.56 × 0.50 biogenic
notes: RDF/SRF (Refuse Derived Fuel/Substitute Recovered Fuel) input — somewhat higher fossil fraction vs. household MSW. Located in Knapsack chemical park near Cologne/Hürth. Co-located industrial heat users. No CCS confirmed.

name: AVG Köln RMVA (Restmüllverbrennungsanlage)
capacity_note: ~900,000 t/yr (Germany's highest-throughput WtE); ~87 MWe; Cologne-Niehl port area
operator: AVG Abfallentsorgungs- und Verwertungsgesellschaft Köln mbH (Stadtwerke Köln)
source: AVG Köln website; GEM Wiki AVG Köln RMVA; Superlative Made in Germany AVG article; calc: 900 kt × 0.56 × 0.50 biogenic
notes: Germany's highest-throughput WtE plant by waste processed (~900 kt/yr). Rhine-side location with potential for CO₂ transport via river corridor or pipeline to North Sea storage. No CCS confirmed. NRW state exploring CCS framework — medium retrofit score.

name: MVA Pfaffenwald Stuttgart
capacity_note: ~38 MWe; large MSW throughput; Stuttgart-Münster industrial area
operator: Abfallverwertungsgesellschaft des Landkreises Ludwigsburg mbH (AVL) / AWG Stuttgart
source: GEM Wiki Pfaffenwald power station; CEWEP interactive map; RWTH Aachen WtE Germany status study 2020
notes: One of several Stuttgart-area WtE plants. Baden-Württemberg has several WtE facilities. No CCS plans. Germany has been slow to develop WtE CCS — regulatory uncertainty remains key barrier (KSpG revision still pending full implementation).

name: SYCTOM Ivry-Paris XIII (Centre de Traitement Ivry-Paris 13)
capacity_note: ~720,000 t/yr household waste (largest French WtE facility); steam to CPCU Paris district heating; two furnace-boiler units × 50 t/h
operator: SUEZ (operator since 2011); SYCTOM (Inter-municipal authority owner — 90 municipalities, 6.5 M inhabitants)
source: SUEZ Ivry-Paris XIII reference page; SYCTOM activity report; CEWEP WtE in Paris presentation; SolVair SYCTOM case study
notes: Partly in Paris 13th arrondissement, partly in Ivry-sur-Seine. Largest WtE in Île-de-France and among largest in France. Steam to CPCU (Paris district heating, >500 km pipes). Major renovation/rebuilding project ongoing as of 2020s — new plant planned for ~2030 at this site. New-build could integrate CCS from design.

name: SYCTOM Issy-les-Moulineaux (UVE Issy)
capacity_note: ~460,000 t/yr household waste; 3 furnace lines; suburb of Paris, Hauts-de-Seine
operator: SYCTOM (inter-municipal authority) / operated by Veolia
source: SYCTOM annual statistics; CEWEP France WtE data; calc: 460 kt × 0.56 × 0.50 biogenic
notes: Second major Paris-region SYCTOM plant. No CCS plans. France is building out CCS infrastructure (Dunkirk DUNCO₂ hub, Normandy corridor) but WtE has not been prioritized for near-term. Long-term rebuild plans may enable CCS-readiness.

name: Lagunes de Fos-sur-Mer UVE (Marseille region)
capacity_note: ~420,000 t/yr; Fos-sur-Mer industrial port zone near Marseille
operator: SEM (Société d'Économie Mixte) Énergie Environnement Provence; operated by Suez
source: CEWEP French WtE data; French Ministry of Ecology SINOE waste database; calc: 420 kt × 0.55 × 0.50 biogenic
notes: Located in Fos-sur-Mer (Port of Marseille industrial zone — Marseille-Fos port is among largest in Europe). Industrial cluster has active CCS investigation for cement/steel. Medium retrofit score due to potential integration with emerging Fos-sur-Mer industrial CO₂ cluster.

name: Indaver Doel / SLECO Waste-to-Energy
capacity_note: 1,200,000 t/yr total site; SLECO fluidized-bed: 447,000 t/yr non-hazardous waste + sludge; 3 turbines ~85 MWe total
operator: Indaver NV (SLECO JV: Indaver + Veolia/SUEZ); Indaver holds majority in Doel complex
source: Indaver Doel CEWEP plant visit presentation; GEM Wiki SLECO Waste-to-Energy; Indaver Belgium activities page; Indaver annual data
notes: Doel site: largest integrated waste treatment complex in Belgium, handling 1.2 Mt/yr total. SLECO uses fluidized bed technology (3 units) for sludge + industrial waste — higher biogenic fraction than MSW grate. E-Wood plant (non-recyclable wood waste, 20 MWe) also on-site. Port of Antwerp-Bruges proximity offers CO₂ transport infrastructure access. Belgium has emerging CCS CO₂ hub plans in Antwerp port.

name: ISVAG Wilrijk Antwerp Waste-to-Energy
capacity_note: 200,000 t/yr MSW; ~10.5 MWe; Wilrijk (Antwerp agglomeration)
operator: ISVAG (Intercommunale voor Slib en Vuilverwijdering Antwerpse Gemeenten)
source: ISVAG Dublix Technology reference; IndustryAbout Gent incineration data; ISVAG CEWEP case study; calc: 200 kt × 0.55 × 0.50 biogenic
notes: Inter-municipal plant serving 1+ million Antwerp residents. Smaller capacity than Indaver Doel. Antwerp port CO₂ cluster (ECLUSE initiative, Ineos/Fluxys CCS planning) could make CCS retrofit attractive in mid-2030s despite small scale.

name: IVAGO Gent Waste-to-Energy
capacity_note: 100,000 t/yr MSW; 4.2 MWe; Proeftuinstraat 43, Gent
operator: IVAGO (Inter-municipal association, Gent area)
source: IndustryAbout Gent Incineration Plant; Dublix Technology IVAGO reference; GEM coordinates from Open Infrastructure Map area
notes: Small plant serving Gent area. At 4.2 MWe too small for economical standalone CCS. Potential for network aggregation with larger Flemish WtE plants. Low retrofit score due to small scale.

name: KEZO Hinwil Waste-to-Energy (Kehrichtverwertung Zürcher Oberland)
capacity_note: ~120,000 t/yr MSW; 12.5 MWe; Im Fennen 1a, 8867 Niederurnen (Glarus canton); planning new 2030 MSWI plant
operator: KEZO Zweckverband Kehrichtverwertung Zürcher Oberland
source: KEZO CCS page (kva-linth.ch/energie-umwelt/ccs); Carbon Herald KEZO/Sulzer CO₂ capture pilot; CCUSNetwork KEZO entry; CATACARB HPC pilot press release 2025
notes: CCS PILOT ACTIVE (2025): Sulzer/CATACARB Hot Potassium Carbonate pilot capturing ~1,000 t CO₂/yr for use by adjacent greenhouse. Planning new 2030 MSWI plant — target 120,000 t/yr capture on new plant. Also co-hosts Climeworks first commercial DAC plant (separate facility on same site). High retrofit score as first Swiss WtE with active CCS pilot and new-build integration target.

name: KVA Hagenholz Zürich
capacity_note: ~430,000 t/yr MSW + sewer sludge; ~35 MWe; largest single-site biogenic CO₂ source in Zürich canton
operator: ERZ Entsorgung + Recycling Zürich (City of Zürich)
source: BAFU Swiss CCS & NETs report 2024; ETH DEMO UPCARMA WP4 scaling study; Swiss WtE sewer sludge incinerator pilot documentation
notes: CCS PILOT REPORTED: Hagenholz is the biggest single CO₂ point source in Zürich; city studying CCS. A sewer sludge co-incineration test bed for CO₂ capture technology piloted there is part of plans to equip the much larger Hagenholz main waste incinerator. Swiss BAFU/ETH study identifies Hagenholz as a priority site for CCUS chain scale-up. High retrofit score due to active planning and scale.

name: KVA Linth (Kehrichtverwertungsanlage Linthgebiet)
capacity_note: 120,000 t/yr MSW; 12.5 MWe; planning new 2030 MSWI facility; Niederurnen, Glarus
operator: Zweckverband Kehrichtverwertung Linthgebiet (KEZO and KVA Linth are two different Glarus/Zürich Oberland plants)
source: KVA Linth website; CCUS Network KVA Linth entry; Sulzer/KEZO pilot (different but adjacent plant); opendata.swiss KVA geodata
notes: Separate plant from KEZO Hinwil. KVA Linth also studying CCS integration for the planned 2030 new facility. Switzerland's CO₂ law and net-zero pathway explicitly include WtE CCS as a negative emission measure. High retrofit score for CCS readiness in new-build plan.

name: Wien Energie Spittelau Waste-to-Energy
capacity_note: ~250,000 t/yr MSW; ~85 MWth thermal; 60,000 households district heating; Vienna 9th district (Hundertwasser building)
operator: Wien Energie GmbH (City of Vienna 100% owned)
source: Wien Energie Spittelau pages; GreenEnergyLab Spittelau heat project; Waste-to-Energy World article 50 years Hundertwasser incinerator
notes: Iconic Hundertwasser-designed building; Vienna landmark. Mainly district heating (60,000+ households). Small electrical output (~40,000 MWh/yr). Low retrofit score due to urban setting, small scale, and no announced CCS plans. Austria lacks CO₂ storage infrastructure; low national CCS policy priority.

name: Energie AG Wels Waste-to-Energy
capacity_note: 300,000+ t/yr residual waste (2 lines); 100% district heat for Wels city (14,800 households)
operator: Energie AG Umwelt Service GmbH (Energie AG Oberösterreich subsidiary)
source: INP International Projects AVE Wels reference; Energie AG Umwelt Service district heat Wels report; Austrian WtE whitebook
notes: Upper Austria. Operational since 1991. Supplies 100% of Wels district heating. Two incineration lines. Austria has no CO₂ storage infrastructure — all WtE plants are low retrofit score. Some discussion of CO₂ use (greenhouses, food & beverage) but no geological storage pathway.

name: TERSA Sant Adrià de Besòs (Barcelona Waste-to-Energy)
capacity_note: 360,000 t/yr MSW (3 lines); ~200,000 MWh/yr electricity; Sant Adrià del Besòs, Barcelona metropolitan area
operator: TERSA (Tractament i Eliminació de Residus SA) — public company (AMB/Barcelona)
source: Grup Tersa waste-to-energy page; Lab.fr Barcelona WtE plant profile; SICK TERSA emission measurement case study; ResearchGate LCA 2022
notes: Barcelona Metropolitan Area public company. Inaugurated 1975, rebuilt 1997. Three treatment lines. No CCS plans. Spain has very limited CO₂ storage infrastructure; no policy framework for WtE CCS. Low retrofit score.

name: Zabalgarbi Bilbao Waste-to-Energy
capacity_note: ~540,000 t/yr MSW + industrial waste; ~57 MWe (waste fraction, gas turbine add ~50 MWe); Basque Country
operator: Zabalgarbi S.A. (FCC Medio Ambiente + Diputación Foral de Vizcaya JV)
source: Zabalgarbi data-of-interest page; GEM Wiki Zabalgarbi power station; FCC Medio Ambiente WtE page; ScienceDirect exergy analysis case study
notes: Hybrid WtE + gas turbine plant (combined cycle). MSW fraction provides ~300,000–400,000 t/yr waste, supplemented by natural gas combined cycle for higher efficiency. Annual net: ~650 GWh. No CCS plans. Basque Country has CCS research but no active WtE CCS projects.

name: A2A Brescia Lamarmora Waste-to-Energy
capacity_note: ~750,000 t/yr MSW (total Brescia WtE complex); ~85–117 MWe; one of the largest WtE complexes in Italy
operator: A2A S.p.A. (formerly ASM Brescia / AEM Brescia)
source: GEO Global Energy Observatory Brescia WtE (geoid/2429); A2A WtE plants page; ESG News A2A $120M sustainability investment; CEWEP A2A flue gas condensation
notes: Brescia WtE is a CHP complex (electricity + district heating for Bergamo, Brescia, Milan networks). A2A investing €120M for sustainability/efficiency upgrades. Italy developing CO₂ storage framework for offshore Adriatic storage (ENI CCS projects). A2A has expressed interest in net-zero but no WtE CCS announcement. Medium retrofit score.

name: A2A Silla 2 Milano Waste-to-Energy
capacity_note: 550,000 t/yr MSW (3 lines); ~59 MWe; northwest Milan near Figino
operator: A2A Ambiente S.p.A. (A2A Group)
source: GEM Wiki Silla 2 power station; Silla 2 municipality Milan page; Technital Silla 2 project profile; ValveIT Silla 2 project sheet
notes: Three identical combustion lines with mobile grate technology. CHP — electricity + Milan district heating. Municipality of Milan is a shareholder in A2A. No confirmed CCS plans. ENI Ravenna hub (offshore Adriatic) could eventually serve northern Italy WtE clusters.

name: Acea Ambiente San Vittore del Lazio Waste-to-Energy
capacity_note: ~650,000 t/yr MSW (3 lines); ~49 MWe total (13.9 MWe line 1 + 17.5 MWe × 2 lines); Lazio's largest WtE
operator: Acea Ambiente S.r.l. (Acea Group; partial Roma Capitale ownership)
source: Acea Group San Vittore plant page; Acea Ambiente a-ambiente.it San Vittore plant; Acea annual sustainability reports 2022–2023
notes: Frosinone province (southeast of Rome). Largest WtE in Lazio. Three processing lines. Acea Group is Rome's public utility. No CCS plans. Central Italy has limited onshore CO₂ storage; offshore central/southern Italy storage potential is under early assessment (ENI).

name: Attero Moerdijk Waste-to-Energy (AEC Moerdijk)
capacity_note: 1,045,000 t/yr MSW (4 incineration lines); ~125 MWe; Moerdijk industrial port
operator: Attero B.V. (The Circular Company; previously AVR)
source: IndustryAbout Moerdijk Incineration Plant; GEM Wiki AEC Moerdijk; Power-Technology Moerdijk WtE profile; Attero locations page
notes: One of the largest WtE plants in Europe. CHP + large electricity export. Port of Moerdijk gives excellent CO₂ transport access to North Sea storage via Rotterdam CO₂ corridor (Porthos project). Attero publishes sustainability targets — exploring CCS pathways. High retrofit score: scale + port infrastructure + Netherlands CCS policy leadership.

name: HVC Alkmaar Waste-to-Energy
capacity_note: ~1,200,000 t/yr MSW (~68–93 MWe); Boekelermeer polder, Alkmaar, North Holland
operator: HVC N.V. (100% public; 49 municipalities + 6 water boards in North Holland/Flevoland)
source: Power-Technology HVC Alkmaar WtE profile; GEM Wiki HVC Alkmaar; EIB project 20060306 (HVC Alkmaar Biomass); ABB Migrating Dutch WtE reference
notes: One of the largest WtE plants in the Netherlands by waste throughput. Also has co-located biomass CHP unit. Public ownership by 49 municipalities aligns with Dutch WtE CCS policy goals. Amsterdam-Alkmaar industrial corridor — potential CO₂ transport pipeline access. High retrofit score.

name: ARN B.V. Nijmegen Waste-to-Energy (Weurt)
capacity_note: ~410,000 t/yr MSW; 27 MWe + 800 TJ/yr heat (6,400 homes); Weurt, Gelderland
operator: ARN B.V. (regional public waste authority)
source: Power-Technology ARN Nijmegen WtE; TRIA International ARN profile; ARN B.V. IkNijmegen listing; Gelderland waste authority annual data
notes: Operational since 1987. Weurt (Beuningen municipality, near Nijmegen). Diaper recycling pioneering project. Netherlands CCS policy actively supports WtE CCS — ARN is a candidate for future Porthos network extension or regional CO₂ collection point.

name: KHK Kraków Eco-Incinerator (ZTPOK)
capacity_note: 220,000 t/yr MSW; 32 MWe + district heat; POSCO E&C constructed; operational 2016
operator: KHK S.A. (Krakowski Holding Komunalny — city-owned)
source: EC Regional Policy Kraków WtE project; IntechOpen Kraków WtE case study; CEWEP Kraków plant control article; CCS4Krakow project page; POSCO E&C completion press release
notes: CCS4KRAKOW PROJECT: Active EU/Norway-funded feasibility study (CCS4Krakow.eu) exploring CO₂ capture, transport, and storage from this plant. Poland-Norway bilateral programme. First Polish WtE plant with active CCS investigation. Medium retrofit score due to early-stage feasibility rather than FID.

name: ITPOK Poznań Energy from Waste
capacity_note: 210,000 t/yr MSW; ~17.6 MWe + 34 MW district heat; operational 2016; Suez Zielona Energia operated
operator: Suez Zielona Energia sp. z o.o. (SUEZ; Marguerite fund infrastructure)
source: Suez Zielona Energia ITPOK page; Kanadevia-Inova Poznań reference; Power-Technology Poznan EfW; EIB Poznan EfW PPP case study
notes: Kanadevia (Hitachi Zosen) grate technology. 2 × 13.2 t/h lines, 63 MW thermal. PPP project with Marguerite infrastructure fund. Poland developing national CCS strategy but no WtE-specific framework. Operational efficiently — potential future network node.

name: ZTPOK Bydgoszcz Waste-to-Energy
capacity_note: ~180,000 t/yr MSW; ~13 MWe; operational 2016; ProNatura operated
operator: ProNatura sp. z o.o. (REMONDIS group)
source: Power-Technology Bydgoszcz WtE profile; Termomeccanica WtE Bydgoszcz reference; MDPI Energy Efficiency Polish WtE analysis 2024
notes: Thermomeccanica grate technology. Medium capacity among Polish plants. Part of Kuyavia-Pomerania region. No CCS plans. Poland's WtE fleet is newer (all post-2013) but coal-heavy national energy system reduces policy urgency for WtE CCS.

name: Mercer Stendal Kraft Pulp Mill (Zellstoff Stendal)
capacity_note: 740,000 t/yr NBSK pulp; 148 MWe green electricity; Arneburg on Elbe River, Saxony-Anhalt
operator: Mercer International Inc. (Mercer Stendal GmbH)
source: Mercer International Stendal operations page; GEM Wiki Stendal Mill power station; Mercer annual reports; calc: 740 kt × 0.92 t CO₂/adt × 1.0 (pulp and energy boiler combined)
notes: One of the largest single-line kraft pulp mills in Europe by capacity. 148 MWe biomass power plant — one of Germany's largest biomass electricity generators. Elbe River location. No CCS announced. Germany pulp mills (also Rosenthal) identified in academic BECCS potential studies as major biogenic CO₂ sources. Medium retrofit score.

name: Mercer Rosenthal Kraft Pulp Mill
capacity_note: 360,000 t/yr NBSK pulp; ~400,000 MWh/yr green electricity; Rosenthal am Rennsteig, Thuringia
operator: Mercer International Inc. (Mercer Rosenthal GmbH)
source: Mercer Rosenthal operations page; AFRY climate-neutral pulp production study; Canadian Biomass Magazine Mercer emissions article; calc: 360 kt × 0.92 t CO₂/adt
notes: Thuringian Forest location. Mercer is extracting lignin from black liquor at pilot scale (1 t/day). AFRY study on path to climate-neutral pulp production cites Rosenthal as key German site. Lime kiln conversion from fossil fuels to renewable energy under study. No CCS confirmed at German mills.

name: Sappi Ehingen Pulp & Paper Mill
capacity_note: ~160,000 t/yr dissolved sulphite pulp (HW+SW); integrated paper mill; Danube River, Baden-Württemberg
operator: Sappi Europe S.A. (Sappi Ltd, South Africa)
source: Sappi Ehingen Mill factsheet; Sappi Ehingen EMAS report 2024; Sappi ratcheting-up pulp integration article
notes: World's first chlorine-free bleaching plant. ~85% of primary energy from biogenic fuels (black liquor, biogas, bark). Danube River location. Sulphite pulp not kraft — smaller recovery boiler CO₂ stream than kraft mills. Sappi has sustainability program but no CCS announced. The mill is smaller than major kraft mills but has very high biogenic energy fraction.

name: Sappi Alfeld Pulp & Paper Mill
capacity_note: ~127,750 t/yr dissolved sulphite pulp; integrated paper mill; Leine River, Lower Saxony
operator: Sappi Europe S.A.
source: Sappi Alfeld Mill page; Sappi Alfeld restructure consultation 2024; pulp-paperworld.com PM2 rebuild article
notes: Near Hanover. Five digesters × 250 m³. ~350 t/day pulp. Sappi Alfeld is under restructuring review (consultation announced 2024) — potential capacity reduction or closure risk. Lower retrofit score due to business uncertainty and smaller scale. Sulphite process.

name: Fibre Excellence Tarascon Pulp Mill (Provence)
capacity_note: ~220,000 t/yr bleached kraft pulp (BHKP); Chemin des Radoubs, 13156 Tarascon, Bouches-du-Rhône
operator: Fibre Excellence Group (privately held; supported by Caisse des Dépôts)
source: Fibre Excellence Provence mill page; EIB EUR 40M loan to Navigator Figueira da Foz (separate, used as comp); EUWID Tarascon secured article; Fibre Excellence €190M decarbonization investment plan 2027 ('Choose France')
notes: South of France, on Rhône River. Fibre Excellence committed to €190M investment by 2027 (France national industrial investment program) for fluff pulp expansion and decarbonization. Rhône River corridor could facilitate CO₂ transport to Mediterranean offshore storage or Dunkirk/Normandy storage via future pipeline network.

name: Fibre Excellence Saint-Gaudens Pulp Mill
capacity_note: ~280,000 t/yr kraft pulp; Haute-Garonne (Occitanie), south of France
operator: Fibre Excellence Group
source: Fibre Excellence Saint-Gaudens mill page; EUWID Saint-Gaudens articles (production interruptions 2021, resumption 2023); paper-world.com Fibre Excellence Saint-Gaudens
notes: Pyrénées foothills location. Resumed production 2023 after major maintenance/modernization stop. No CCS plans. Remote from French CO₂ transport infrastructure. Lower retrofit score than Tarascon due to inland location and intermittent operational history.

name: Mondi Frantschach Kraft Pulp & Sack Paper Mill
capacity_note: ~280,000 t/yr sack kraft paper + speciality market pulp; Frantschach-Sankt Gertraud, Carinthia
operator: Mondi Frantschach GmbH (Mondi Group)
source: Mondi Group Frantschach location page; Mondi Frantschach €20M investment press release 2021; Andritz spectrum Frantschach recovery boiler start-up
notes: Carinthia valley location. Mondi Frantschach is one of the world's most advanced sack kraft paper mills. Energy self-sufficient for many years; exports heat to communities. Uses ~1.4M m³ pulpwood/yr. No CCS. Austria has no CO₂ storage sites. Low retrofit score.

name: Sappi Gratkorn Pulp & Paper Mill
capacity_note: ~250,000 t/yr kraft pulp + 950,000 t/yr coated paper; River Mur, north of Graz, Styria
operator: Sappi Europe S.A.
source: Sappi Gratkorn Mill page; Sappi co-creating coal-to-renewables shift at Gratkorn; Paper Age Gratkorn biomass 2023; energy-innovation-austria biomass article
notes: €35M investment converted power plant boiler to 100% biomass (300,000 t/yr biomass required) — ~30% CO₂ footprint reduction. Biomass conversion complete ~2022. River Mur location. Austria lacks CO₂ storage. Low retrofit score despite active sustainability investment.

name: Zellstoff Pöls (Heinzel Group) Kraft Pulp Mill
capacity_note: ~430,000 t/yr pulp + ~80,000 t/yr bleached kraft paper; Pöls (Tauernstraße 15, 8761 Pöls), Styria; expansion to >500,000 t announced
operator: Zellstoff Pöls AG (Heinzel Group; Heinzel Holding Austria)
source: Heinzel Group expansion announcement; Andritz Pöls largest new paper machine (PM2 startup); Manufacturing Today Zellstoff Pöls; Heinzelpoels.com About us
notes: Styria, near Judenburg. Heinzel Group investing in major capacity expansion (>500,000 t/yr pulp). New paper machine PM2 from Andritz started up 2024 — Europe's largest new paper machine. Despite large scale, Austria's absence of CO₂ storage keeps retrofit score low. Pulp expansion increases biogenic CO₂ significantly.

name: Navigator Company Figueira da Foz Pulp & Paper Mill
capacity_note: ~570,000 t/yr BEKP pulp + ~800,000 t/yr UWF paper; Figueira da Foz, Coimbra district, coast
operator: The Navigator Company S.A.
source: Navigator Company Figueira da Foz mill page; EIB EUR 40M loan 2018 (energy efficiency); EUWID storm damage 2024; Navigator SEC filings; calc: 570 kt × 0.92 t CO₂/adt
notes: Coastal location on Atlantic — good for future offshore CO₂ storage via Portuguese offshore basins (Lusitanian Basin) or potential Atlantic transport. Integrated pulp+paper mill. Navigator announced decarbonization roadmap but no CCS. Portugal is developing offshore CCS framework. Medium retrofit score for coastal access.

name: Navigator Company Setúbal Pulp Mill
capacity_note: ~550,000 t/yr BEKP pulp; Setúbal, Setúbal district, Sado estuary
operator: The Navigator Company S.A.
source: Navigator Company Wikipedia; Navigator-USA corporate PDF; Navigator investors PDF; calc: 550 kt × 0.92 t CO₂/adt
notes: Setúbal (south of Lisbon). Industrial port area on Sado estuary. Located near the Portimão industrial corridor and Sines port (Portugal's main deep-water port and potential CO₂ export terminal). Medium retrofit score — coastal + port access gives good future CCS transport options.

name: Altri Celbi Pulp Mill (Leirosa)
capacity_note: ~800,000 t/yr BEKP pulp (world record production lines); Leirosa, Figueiró dos Vinhos municipality, coastal
operator: Celbi S.A. (Altri SGPS group)
source: Celbi website production capacity; Andritz Celbi world record article; Altri SGPS investor relations; calc: 800 kt × 0.92 t CO₂/adt
notes: Leirosa, Figueiró dos Vinhos, coastal Coimbra district. One of the most efficient global eucalyptus pulp producers (multiple Andritz world records). Atlantic coastal location. No CCS announced but Altri Group has active sustainability targets. Same coastal advantages as Navigator Figueira da Foz.

name: Ence Navia Biofactory (Pulp Mill)
capacity_note: 685,000 t/yr ECF eucalyptus pulp (post-Navia 80 expansion); Navia estuary, Asturias
operator: Ence Energía y Celulosa S.A.
source: Ence Navia Biofactory page; Andritz Ence Navia 80 expansion article; Ence AGM 2025 biogenic CO₂ statement (>4 Mt/yr total); calc: 685 kt × 0.92 t CO₂/adt
notes: Post-expansion to 685,000 t/yr (Navia 80 project via Andritz). Ence claims >4 Mt/yr biogenic CO₂ potential across both mills — working on CO₂ capture engineering + green hydrogen + synthetic fuels for maritime/aviation. Navia estuary location; no CO₂ storage in Spain — CCU pathway more likely than CCS.

name: Ence Pontevedra Biofactory (Pulp Mill)
capacity_note: 515,000 t/yr BEK eucalyptus pulp; Ría de Pontevedra estuary, Galicia
operator: Ence Energía y Celulosa S.A.
source: Ence Pontevedra Biofactory page; Ence AGM 2025; Environmental Paper Network Spain case study Mar 2025
notes: Controversial urban location in Pontevedra estuary — court rulings have challenged the operating licence (relocation under discussion as of 2025). Uncertainty about long-term site viability reduces retrofit score below Navia. Ence CCU plans apply to both mills.

name: Mondi Świecie Containerboard & Pulp Mill
capacity_note: ~600,000 t/yr bleached + unbleached pulp; 6 paper machines; major Kujawsko-Pomorskie industrial site
operator: Mondi Świecie S.A. (Mondi Group)
source: Mondi Świecie S.A. CEWEP/seat document; Mondi €95M investment completion 2024; Andritz major pulp capacity increase at Mondi Świecie; GEM Wiki Swiecie Mill power station
notes: Largest integrated pulp and containerboard mill in Poland. €95M investment completed 2024 (new PM, recycled fibre line, energy recovery upgrade). CHP with significant biomass fraction. Poland developing CCS strategy; Mondi has SBTi net-zero targets. Medium retrofit score — large source, active investment, but Poland CCS infrastructure nascent.

name: Mayr-Melnhof / IP Kwidzyn Pulp & Paperboard Mill
capacity_note: ~400,000 t/yr kraft pulp + ~740,000 t/yr paperboard/UFS on 4 paper machines; Kwidzyn, Pomerania
operator: Mayr-Melnhof Karton AG (acquired from International Paper 2021, EUR 670M)
source: Papnews IP Kwidzyn sale to MM; PRNewswire IP completes sale; Mayr-Melnhof Karton acquisition press release; calc: 400 kt × 0.92 t CO₂/adt
notes: Formerly International Paper's largest European mill. Sold to Mayr-Melnhof 2021. Largest integrated pulp+paper mill in Poland by paper output. Pulp production ~400 kt/yr market + fluff. MM Karton has sustainability program but no CCS plans. Low retrofit score — ownership transition, no CCS policy framework in Poland for mills.

name: Arctic Paper Kostrzyn nad Odrą Paper & Pulp Mill
capacity_note: ~315,000 t/yr uncoated woodfree paper + integrated pulp production; Kostrzyn nad Odrą, Western Poland
operator: Arctic Paper S.A. (listed, Swedish-controlled)
source: Arctic Paper Kostrzyn mill page; EUWID capacity expansion article; GEM Wiki Kostrzyn paper mill power station; paper-world.com Arctic Paper Kostrzyn
notes: Western Poland on Oder River — border with Germany. Integrated pulp-paper mill. Largest offset paper producer in Poland. No CCS. Proximity to Germany could facilitate future cross-border CO₂ transport if German CCS infrastructure expands.

name: Mondi Štětí Pulp & Paper Mill
capacity_note: ~600,000 t/yr bleached/unbleached pulp + 210,000 t/yr new kraft paper (PM added 2024); Štětí, Ústecký Region, Elbe River
operator: Mondi Štětí a.s. (Mondi Group)
source: Mondi Štětí location page; GEM Wiki Mondi Steti power station; Papnews 70 years article; Mondi €470M modernisation plan; packaging-gateway new PM article; coordinates from Open Infrastructure Map (50.46091835, 14.37585352)
notes: Czech Republic's largest paper mill (70+ years history). New 210,000 t/yr kraft paper machine started 2024 (€470M modernization). Two fibre lines. Located on Elbe River — potential CO₂ transport corridor northward to North Sea storage. Mondi SBTi targets. Medium retrofit score.

name: Mondi SCP Ružomberok Pulp & Paper Mill
capacity_note: ~580,000 t/yr uncoated fine paper + ~310,000 t/yr containerboard + 100,000 t/yr market pulp; Ružomberok, Žilina region
operator: Mondi SCP a.s. (Mondi Group)
source: Mondi SCP Slovakia location page; Andritz ANDRITZ spectrum 31 Ružomberok; Mondi SBTi targets 2022; Open Infrastructure Map coordinates (49.0786326, 19.3338346); Mondi new biomass power plant 2025 announcement
notes: Slovakia's largest integrated pulp and paper mill. New biomass power plant announced 2025 (Mondi) to increase energy self-sufficiency to 90% — reduces fossil CO₂ but increases biogenic CO₂ throughput. Slovakia has no CO₂ storage infrastructure. Low retrofit score despite large biogenic source.

name: Mercer Stendal Biomass Power (co-located with pulp mill)
capacity_note: 148 MWe biomass/bioenergy CHP — power sold to grid; bark, wood residues, black liquor energy recovery
operator: Mercer International Inc. (Mercer Stendal GmbH) — power plant is co-registered with pulp operations
source: GEM Wiki Stendal Mill power station; Mercer International Stendal page (148 MWe figure); Germany biogenic CO₂ dynamics study PMC 2024
notes: Co-located with Mercer Stendal pulp mill (separate entry). The 148 MWe power plant is one of Germany's largest biomass electricity generators. Black liquor recovery boiler is dominant CO₂ source. High biogenic CO₂ concentration in flue gas. Academic BECCS studies (Springer, PMC 2024) list Stendal among Germany's top priority kraft BECCS sites.

name: UPM Augsburg Paper Mill (biomass CHP)
capacity_note: Europe's largest paper mill site; ~1,600,000 t/yr paper; CHP plant providing process energy; biomass fraction significant
operator: UPM Communication Papers GmbH (UPM-Kymmene)
source: UPM Augsburg mill page; UPM Augsburg CHP inauguration Nov 2022; UPM EMAS report 2024 Augsburg; GEM Wiki Augsburg Mill power station
notes: New state-of-the-art CHP inaugurated November 2022. Europe's largest paper mill by volume. Note: UPM Augsburg is primarily a paper mill using purchased pulp (no kraft recovery boiler) — biogenic CO₂ from biomass CHP + paper process is moderate. No CCS planned. UPM has Finnish BECCS activities but German plants not in current scope.

name: Energie AG Wien Simmering Biomass CHP
capacity_note: ~66 MWe + district heat; dedicated biomass (wood chips) CHP; Vienna-Simmering industrial zone
operator: Wien Energie GmbH (City of Vienna); Waste2Value initiative
source: Wien Smart City Waste2Value project; Siemens Energy Wien Energie waste-to-energy reference; Wien Energie CHP portfolio
notes: Vienna Simmering industrial corridor. Large biomass CHP for district heating and electricity. Part of Wien Energie's decarbonization program. Austria lacks CO₂ storage — low retrofit score. Potential long-term: CO₂ pipeline to Adriatic/North Sea via CEF infrastructure.

name: Attero Wilp Biogas & Bio-LNG Plant
capacity_note: Biogas from VFG (vegetable/fruit/garden) waste; Bio-LNG plant opened Sep 2024 (Queen Máxima inauguration); Wilp, Gelderland
operator: Attero B.V. / Nordsol (Bio-LNG plant is Nordsol technology)
source: Nordsol Wilp case study; Attero Wilp location page; Attero Bio-LNG inauguration Sep 2024
notes: VFG (biowaste) anaerobic digestion produces biogas → upgraded to biomethane → Nordsol liquefies to Bio-LNG. CO₂ stream from upgrading (~35–45% of raw biogas by volume) is near-pure biogenic stream. Currently vented or sold for food/beverage use. Netherlands CCS policy supportive — biogas upgrading CO₂ streams are identified as low-cost CCS candidates. Medium retrofit score: pure CO₂ stream, supportive policy, but small scale.

name: German Biogas Cluster — Bayern/Baden-Württemberg Agricultural AD
capacity_note: ~9,500 agricultural biogas plants in Germany (>50% in Bavaria/BW/NRW); total ~8 GW installed; aggregated CO₂ from upgrading ~2–5 Mt/yr nationally
operator: Multiple operators (municipal, agricultural cooperatives, ENGIE, EnBW, BayWa r.e., etc.)
source: German Biogas Association (Fachverband Biogas) 2024 statistics; DENA biogas atlas; IEA Bioenergy Task 37 Germany; calc: representative largest plant cluster
notes: This entry represents the aggregated opportunity from Germany's ~650 biomethane upgrading plants (out of 9,500 total biogas). Each upgrading plant emits ~1,000–10,000 t CO₂/yr as near-pure biogenic stream. Individual plants too small for standalone CCS — aggregation networks (e.g., Thüga, WINGAS pipeline clusters) needed. BMWK studying biogas-to-BECCS pathways (2024 report). Centroid approx. southern Germany high-density zone. Coordinates represent cluster centroid, not a single plant.

name: Italian Biogas Cluster — Po Valley Agricultural AD
capacity_note: ~1,600 biogas plants in Italy (~1.4 GW); >60% in Po Valley (Lombardia, Veneto, Emilia-Romagna); cattle/pig manure + energy crops
operator: Multiple (cooperatives, large farms, Agrinord, Bioenergia Fiemme, Snam/ENI biomethane offtake)
source: CIB (Consorzio Italiano Biogas) 2024 report; GSE Italy biogas statistics; IEA Bioenergy Task 37 Italy chapter
notes: Po Valley biogas cluster is second-largest in EU after Germany. Snam is developing biomethane-to-grid infrastructure. ENI's Ravenna offshore CCS hub (under development) could eventually receive biogenic CO₂ from upgraded Po Valley biogas — creating a regional BECCS value chain. Centroid approx. Cremona area. Coordinates represent cluster centroid.

name: EnviTec Biogas Güstrow Biomethane Plant
capacity_note: ~80 GWh/yr biomethane (one of Germany's largest single agricultural AD + upgrading plants); cattle slurry + silage; Güstrow, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern
operator: EnviTec Biogas AG (listed; Deutsche Biogas/Envitec subsidiary)
source: EnviTec Biogas AG annual report; German Biogas Association plant register; IEA Bioenergy Task 37 Germany country report
notes: Representative large German agricultural biomethane plant. Güstrow area has multiple EnviTec/NAWARO facilities. CO₂ from biogas upgrading is near-pure biogenic stream — currently vented or sold commercially. Germany's planned biogas strategy (2024 BMWK) is developing frameworks for CO₂ capture from upgrading plants. Small scale per site — aggregation needed for economical CCS.
